arguments.name: d
arguments.text: A matrix with two columns, the two variables. Further columns are ignored.

arguments.name: w
arguments.text: Weight for each row. The default gives every row the same weight. The weights are scaled by their sum, so they need not sum to 1.

origin.details: The coefficient is the weighted covariance divided by the product of the weighted standard deviations, using moments around the weighted means. sum(w) is the sum of the supplied weight vector. This form is the one used for numerical differentiation and for ABC intervals.
origin.value: The correlation between column 1 and column 2.

arguments.name: d
arguments.text: Array with two columns, the two variables. Further columns are ignored.

arguments.name: w
arguments.text: Weight for each row. None gives every row weight 1/n. The weights are scaled by their sum, so they need not sum to 1.

translation.details: The coefficient is the weighted covariance divided by the product of the weighted standard deviations, using moments around the weighted means. The divisor is the sum of the supplied weight vector. Products recycle a shorter argument the way R does.
translation.value: The correlation between column 1 and column 2.
translation.example:
from boot.util import corr

d = [[1, 2], [2, 4], [3, 5], [4, 4], [5, 5]]
print(corr(d))
print(corr(d, w=[1, 1, 1, 1, 5]))
